description: VERUS_SQL_COVERAGE task L: LIKE (default and explicit ESCAPE, NULLs, escape errors, multibyte _ and escape, char(n) padding seen by LIKE), SUBSTRING (start <= 0, negative length 22011, int4-extreme bounds, multibyte, char(n) argument), EXTRACT YEAR/MONTH/DAY from date and timestamp, including BC results reached by interval arithmetic (the GenDB fixture loader reads astronomical ISO dates only). Error cases filter one row by id so the failing expression is evaluated per row (no constant folding).

cases.name: like_default
cases.sql: SELECT id, t LIKE p AS m FROM lk WHERE id < 30
cases.note: Default escape backslash: % any sequence, _ one character (multibyte e-acute is one), escaped wildcards, escaped ordinary characters, C-collation case sensitivity, NULL operands.

cases.name: like_where
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM lk WHERE t LIKE p AND id < 30
cases.note: LIKE as a condition (OfBool): NULL is Unknown and drops the row.

cases.name: not_like_where
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM lk WHERE t NOT LIKE p AND id < 30
cases.note: NOT LIKE = Not(OfBool(Like)): NULL rows are dropped by both.

cases.name: like_trailing_escape
cases.sql: SELECT id, t LIKE p AS m FROM lk WHERE id = 30
cases.note: Pattern 'abc\' ending in the escape: PostgreSQL's matcher exhausts the text first and never reaches the dangling escape, so FALSE, not 22025 (lazy error).

cases.name: like_escape
cases.sql: SELECT id, t LIKE p ESCAPE x AS m FROM lke WHERE id < 20
cases.note: Explicit ESCAPE: '#', '' (no escape: backslash is literal), '%' and '_' as escape (escape wins over the wildcard), multibyte escape, NULL subject/pattern/escape.

cases.name: like_escape_too_long
cases.sql: SELECT id, t LIKE p ESCAPE x AS m FROM lke WHERE id = 20
cases.note: Escape string of two characters: invalid escape string.

cases.name: like_escape_too_long_null_subject
cases.sql: SELECT id, t LIKE p ESCAPE x AS m FROM lke WHERE id = 21
cases.note: NULL subject with an invalid escape: does PostgreSQL check the escape (like_escape(p, x) is evaluated as the operator's argument) before the strict LIKE sees the NULL?

cases.name: like_escape_too_long_null_pattern
cases.sql: SELECT id, t LIKE p ESCAPE x AS m FROM lke WHERE id = 22
cases.note: NULL pattern with an invalid escape: like_escape is strict, so NULL without an error.

cases.name: like_escape_trailing
cases.sql: SELECT id, t LIKE p ESCAPE x AS m FROM lke WHERE id = 23
cases.note: Pattern ending in the explicit escape: like_escape does not reject it; the matcher does not reach it here, so FALSE.

cases.name: like_bpchar_padding
cases.sql: SELECT id, c LIKE 'ab' AS a, c LIKE 'ab%' AS b, c LIKE 'ab__' AS c4, c LIKE 'ab  ' AS d, m LIKE 'é__' AS e, m LIKE 'é_' AS f FROM bp
cases.note: char(n) LIKE: bpcharlike sees the value blank-padded to n characters (GenDB: PadBpchar).

cases.name: like_bpchar_where_not
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM bp WHERE c NOT LIKE 'ab'
cases.note: char(4) 'ab' is 'ab  ' for LIKE, so NOT LIKE 'ab' keeps it.

cases.name: like_varchar_tpch_shapes
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM bp WHERE v LIKE '%BRASS' OR v LIKE 'forest%' OR v NOT LIKE 'MEDIUM POLISHED%'
cases.note: TPC-H pattern shapes on varchar (Q2, Q20, Q16).

cases.name: substring3
cases.sql: SELECT id, SUBSTRING(t FROM st FOR ln) AS r FROM ss WHERE id < 20
cases.note: start <= 0 shortens the result, start + len beyond int4 means 'to the end', start past the end is empty, multibyte characters, NULL operands.

cases.name: substring2
cases.sql: SELECT id, SUBSTRING(t FROM st) AS r FROM ss WHERE id < 20
cases.note: Two-argument form.

cases.name: substring_negative_length
cases.sql: SELECT id, SUBSTRING(t FROM st FOR ln) AS r FROM ss WHERE id = 20
cases.note: Negative length: 22011.

cases.name: substring_negative_length_null
cases.sql: SELECT id, SUBSTRING(t FROM st FOR ln) AS r FROM ss WHERE id = 21
cases.note: Strict: a NULL string gives NULL before the length check.

cases.name: substring_bpchar
cases.sql: SELECT id, SUBSTRING(c FROM 1 FOR 3) AS r, SUBSTRING(c FROM 2) AS r2 FROM bp WHERE SUBSTRING(c FROM 1 FOR 2) IN ('ab', 'xy')
cases.note: char(n) argument goes through the implicit rtrim cast to text (Q22 shape: SUBSTRING(c_phone FROM 1 FOR 2) IN (...)).

cases.name: extract_date
cases.sql: SELECT id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dt) AS y, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM dt) AS m, EXTRACT(DAY FROM dt) AS d FROM dd
cases.note: numeric, scale 0; leap day; NULL.

cases.name: extract_timestamp
cases.sql: SELECT id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ts) AS y, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM ts) AS m, EXTRACT(DAY FROM ts) AS d FROM dd
cases.note: Timestamp fields ignore the time of day.

cases.name: extract_bc
cases.sql: SELECT id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dt - INTERVAL '1' YEAR) AS y1, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dt - INTERVAL '3' YEAR) AS y3, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM dt - INTERVAL '3' YEAR) AS m3, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ts - INTERVAL '1' DAY) AS yt, EXTRACT(DAY FROM ts - INTERVAL '1' DAY) AS dt1 FROM dd WHERE id >= 10
cases.note: BC years: astronomical year y <= 0 is reported as y - 1 (no year 0).

cases.name: extract_group
cases.sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dt) AS y, COUNT(*) AS n FROM dd GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dt)
cases.note: Q7/Q9 shape: GROUP BY an EXTRACT (numeric scale-0 key, NULL group).
